question: Do seed time and harvest ever cease?
summary: Genesis 8:22, the Noahic covenant, declares that while the earth remains, "seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease." The Joseph cycle then narrates seven years of famine so severe that famine extends "in all lands" and "over all the face of the earth" (Genesis 41:54, 41:56, 45:11). The same book records a global agricultural failure that the same book had just promised would never occur.

reconcile.connective: Clarke argues the Hebrew phrase rendered "all the face of the earth" in the famine account properly designates that land — Egypt — not the whole globe.

discrepancy.connective: EvilBible.com presses the plain-sense reading: Genesis 8:22 promises the harvest cycle will never cease, yet Genesis 41 and 45 narrate exactly that multi-year cessation.

skeptic.name: Christopher A. Baba (EvilBible.com)
skeptic.work: EvilBible.com, "Biblical Contradictions" — "Do Seed Time and Harvest Ever Cease?"
skeptic.attribution: Christopher A. Baba, ed., EvilBible.com, "Biblical Contradictions"

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), pp. 425-426
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact pairing under the heading 'Seed time and harvest unfailing. Interrupted at times,' citing Gen. viii. 22 against Gen. xli. 54, 56 and xlv. 6, and argues the Hebrew word rendered 'cease' means 'to come to an end,' so a temporary interruption is not precluded — an unbroken succession of seasons is promised, but not necessarily of crops.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: The original, כל פני הארץ col peney haarets, should be translated, all the face of that land, viz., Egypt, as it is explained at the end of the verse.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the summary's quoted 'over all the face of the earth' (Gen 41:56) by arguing the Hebrew phrase designates Egypt, not the globe — countering the global-famine reading that generates the tension with Gen 8:22.
